review_scope: static: retail instructions and emitted candidate listing

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: Extent 0x004CEF30-0x004CEF3A (11 bytes), 3 instructions a1 eceda400 / a3 f0eda400 / c3, reached as the tail-jump target from 0x00402C36 in the startup sequence 0x00402930.

checks.name: cfg_match
checks.rationale: One basic block, zero edges on both sides; the candidate emits exactly one block with no branch, matching retail. A 1/0 shape is the correct answer here, not a degenerate artifact.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: No argument is read; retail touches no stack slot, only the two absolute data words.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.rationale: No call, no stack write. The single side effect is the dword store at 0x004CEF35.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.rationale: The two data addresses 0x00A4EDEC (read) and 0x00A4EDF0 (write) are exactly four bytes apart; the candidate models them as one two-word zero-initialised pair so the linker cannot reorder them.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.rationale: Emitted listing: mov 0x5a7ce0,%eax ; mov %eax,0x5a7ce4 ; ret - read then store to the adjacent dword, same order and same 11-byte shape as retail.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: Retail's eax keeps the copied value and the only caller (the tail jump from 0x00402930, itself called by 0x00401011) does not read it; declared void without changing what the store does.

limitations: Static only; no runtime observation, and the native is unreachable before the 0x00402930 boundary.
Retail symbol unknown, so the name carries the address suffix as an unverified placeholder.
The meaning of the two data words is not established; the copy is transcribed literally.
